source: FAO / Royal University of Agriculture (RUA) / Australian Government AusAID, coconut beetle biological-control trifold leaflet, published 2005
text:
Besides the introduced Asecodes hispinarum wasp, the leaflet lists several other naturally occurring beneficial organisms that help control coconut beetle populations and should be protected in and around coconut plantations rather than killed by broad-spectrum chemical spraying:

- Beauveria bassiana fungus (ផ្សិត Beauveria bassiana) — an insect-pathogenic fungus that infects and kills beetle larvae.
- Metarhizium anisopliae fungus (ផ្សិត Metarhizium anisopliae) — another insect-pathogenic fungus effective against beetle larvae.
- Earwigs (សត្វខ្នុយពីរ) — predatory insects that feed on beetle eggs and young larvae.
- Ants (អង្រែង) — general predators that attack beetle eggs and larvae on the palm crown.
- Other predatory insect groups present in the plantation that also help suppress the beetle population.

Farmer guidance: protect these beneficial species wherever they are found in and around coconut plantations, since they naturally help keep the coconut beetle population under control; avoid practices (especially chemical insecticide spraying) that would kill them along with the pest.
